current.definition: A steady flow of a fluid (usually from natural causes).

rapids.definition: A part of a river where the current is very fast.

waterfall.definition: Water falling from a high place to a lower one.

pool.definition: A small body of standing water (rainwater) or other liquid.

bend.definition: A curved part of a river where its direction changes.

delta.definition: A low triangular area of alluvial deposits where a river divides before entering a larger body of water.

tributary.definition: A smaller river or stream that flows into a larger one.

estuary.definition: The wide part of a river where it nears the sea.

fish.definition: An animal caught with a fishing line or net.
fish.exampleUsage: The fish was identified during the lesson.

frog.definition: A small animal that lives near water and catches insects.
frog.exampleUsage: The frog was identified during the lesson.

turtle.definition: A slow-moving animal with a hard shell.
turtle.exampleUsage: The turtle was identified during the lesson.

heron.definition: Grey or white wading bird with long neck and long legs and (usually) long bill.
heron.exampleUsage: The heron was identified during the lesson.

otter.definition: A swimming mammal with thick fur and a long body that lives near water.

beaver.definition: A large rodent with a flat tail that builds dams in waterways.

dragonfly.definition: A flying insect with a long body and two pairs of wings.
dragonfly.exampleUsage: The dragonfly was identified during the lesson.

duck.definition: Small wild or domesticated web-footed broad-billed swimming bird usually having a depressed body and short legs.
duck.exampleUsage: The duck was identified during the lesson.

salmon.definition: A fish that commonly moves between the sea and freshwater to reproduce.

crayfish.definition: A small freshwater animal resembling a lobster, with claws and a hard shell.

reed.definition: A tall grass-like plant that grows in wet ground or shallow water.

lily-pad.definition: A large, flat leaf of a water lily that floats on the surface of a pond or lake.

cattail.definition: Tall erect herbs with sword-shaped leaves.

algae.definition: Primitive chlorophyll-containing mainly aquatic eukaryotic organisms lacking true stems and roots and leaves.

willow.definition: Any of numerous deciduous trees and shrubs of the genus Salix.

duckweed.definition: Any small or minute aquatic plant of the family Lemnaceae that float on or near the surface of shallow ponds.

water-lily.definition: A striking flower grows above the water on a stalk and may be white, pink, or yellow.

riverside-grass.definition: Grass growing on or beside the bank of a river.

mangrove.definition: A tropical tree or shrub bearing fruit that germinates while still on the tree and having numerous prop roots that eventually form an impenetrable mass and are important in land building.

canoe.definition: A narrow boat moved with a paddle.

kayak.definition: A narrow boat moved with a double-bladed paddle.

raft.definition: A flat floating platform or inflatable boat used on water.

rowboat.definition: A small boat of shallow draft with cross thwarts for seats and rowlocks for oars with which it is propelled.

motorboat.definition: A boat propelled by an internal-combustion engine.

paddleboard.definition: A long buoyant board designed for standing or kneeling while paddling on water.
paddleboard.exampleUsage: The paddleboard was stored at the supervised recreation center.

inner-tube.definition: An air-filled rubber tube placed inside a pneumatic tire, helping the tire support its load.

pontoon.definition: (nautical) a floating structure (as a flat-bottomed boat) that serves as a dock or to support a bridge.

sailboat.definition: A boat moved mainly by the wind acting on its sails.

fishing-boat.definition: A boat built for fishing, often equipped with a live well that keeps its catch alive.
fishing-boat.exampleUsage: The fishing boat was identified during the lesson.

paddle.definition: A short pole with a wide blade used to move a boat.

life-jacket.definition: A sleeveless safety jacket that keeps a person afloat through buoyant material or trapped air.

fishing-rod.definition: A long flexible pole used with a line to catch fish.
fishing-rod.exampleUsage: The fishing rod was identified during the lesson.

tackle-box.definition: A portable case with separate compartments keeps fishing gear organized and easy for anglers to reach.
tackle-box.exampleUsage: The tackle box was identified during the lesson.

net.definition: A net stretched across a court or between players.

bucket.definition: The quantity contained in a bucket.

waders.definition: Any of many long-legged birds that wade in water in search of food.
waders.exampleUsage: The waders was identified during the lesson.

anchor.definition: A presenter who leads a television news program.

rope.definition: A strong cord used for tying or securing things.

cooler.definition: An insulated container used to keep food and drinks cold.

fishing.definition: Catching fish as a sport or activity.
fishing.exampleUsage: The fishing was identified during the lesson.

swimming.definition: Moving through water for exercise or pleasure.

kayaking.definition: The activity of traveling on water in a kayak; conditions and safety support are important.
kayaking.exampleUsage: The river center offers supervised kayaking on suitable days.

rafting.definition: The activity of traveling on a river in an inflatable raft, sometimes through strong currents; professional guidance and safety equipment are important.
rafting.exampleUsage: The commercial rafting trip was led by trained guides.

canoeing.definition: Travelling on water in a narrow boat moved with a paddle.

tubing.definition: Floating along a river while sitting on an inflated tube.

wading.definition: Walking with your feet in shallow water.

bird-watching.definition: Watching birds to identify and enjoy them.
bird-watching.exampleUsage: The bird watching was identified during the lesson.

picnic.definition: Eating a meal outdoors, often on a blanket or table.

skipping-stones.definition: The activity of throwing flat stones across water so they bounce on the surface.
skipping-stones.exampleUsage: They skipped stones from a clear shoreline away from other people.

bank.definition: The sloping earth ground bordering a flowing river channel.

bed.definition: The bottom channel ground over which river water currents flow.
